description: tools.list with available=false — P31's honest third state made listable: `search` and `graph` are tools this build IMPLEMENTS and cannot RUN, because their resolver seams are not wired here. They are listed, with their real schemas and hashes, and `available:false`; they are not omitted (an omission reads as "no such tool" and sends the reader to the wrong screen) and not refused. `conditional:true` says why, and `tools.status`' `counts.conditionalUnwired` is the same two counted from the same single pass over one world.

tools.name: graph
tools.description:
Structural questions about this project's code: who calls what, what a symbol relates to, where a name is declared. Returns SYMBOLS and file:line LOCATIONS, never file contents — read the file for what it says.

Complements `grep`; it does not replace it. For an exact string or a literal pattern use `grep`. For call relations and cross-file structure, this.

Actions: "explain" (one symbol's direct edges, both directions), "path" (the shortest chain between two symbols, bounded), "query" (browse nodes by kind/name-prefix/file). Answers are four-state: found, ambiguous (candidates listed, none picked), not-found, not-built (this project has no index yet — say so rather than concluding the symbol is absent).

file.description: for query: only nodes from this project-relative file

from.description: for path: the chain's start symbol

kind.description: for query: filter by node kind (function, method, type, interface, class, file, package)

symbol.description: for explain: the symbol to explain — bare or qualified (order.Validate)

to.description: for path: the chain's end symbol

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Semantic and keyword search over this project's code or its loop history. Returns file:line locations, never file contents — read the file to see current truth.

Complements `grep`; it does not replace it. For an exact identifier, a literal string, or a definition, use `grep` — it has an exact answer and this does not.

Requires a corpus: "code" or "history". There is no default.

corpus.description: which corpus to search; REQUIRED — there is no default (a default corpus is a query whose scope depends on a setting the caller did not state)

query.description: the question in words; an empty query is refused rather than answered with everything
